# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue with his heart, requiring regular check-ups to monitor its condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with food textures and is picky about what he eats.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, affecting his muscle tone and overall physical strength.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is upset by loud noises and gets frustrated easily in crowded or loud spaces.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia and is adjusting to wearing glasses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak teeth enamel, requiring careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and is behind his peers in terms of overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth enamel and overall dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing and address any concerns.
* Regular eyesight reviews to monitor vision and address any concerns.
* Regular cardiac check-ups to monitor heart condition.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and other concerns.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consideration of referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for any skeletal anomalies.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a known structural abnormality in her heart, requiring regular cardiology appointments for monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, managed through diet adjustments and occasional medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome, with a few requiring short-term or longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out quicker than her peers during physical activities, suggesting potential neurological or muscular issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in some cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is overwhelmed by loud noises and gets frustrated in crowded or noisy environments, suggesting potential hearing or sensory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, which has been an ongoing issue and may affect her schoolwork.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires more frequent dental check-ups due to various issues, including cavities and sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's blurry vision may affect her schoolwork.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans at the secondary level.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or other interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle took longer to close than typical, which was a concern until it finally closed after several years.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia or requiring review for tethered cord.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5, even if earlier reviews give a clear response, to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis, to monitor the known structural heart abnormality.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental and behavioural needs.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, with weaker muscles than expected for her age, and is working with a physiotherapist to help strengthen them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear recently, which was due to a buildup of fluid, and received medication to clear it up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains that things look blurry sometimes, and the cause is currently unknown.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient is not speaking as much as expected for her age, and when she tries to communicate, it can be hard for others to understand what she means.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

Parent: The doctor said there's something structurally wrong with her heart. I don't fully understand it all, but apparently, it's something she was born with. They say it's not life-threatening or anything, but I still worry constantly. What if something happens to her?

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structurally abnormal heart, a condition she was born with, which is not life-threatening but causes concern for the parent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, including an aversion to certain textures and tastes, making mealtime stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted easily, even from simple play, and has a history of a fontanelle that didn't close properly, which sometimes opens too widely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological issues such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had fluid build-up in her ear, affecting her hearing, and has required medical intervention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many have required multiple grommet insertions.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, especially when looking at distant objects, causing concern about her vision and safety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing due to hard foods and requires food to be cut into small pieces or cooked until soft.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may transfer to special schooling or require Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a history of a fontanelle that didn't close properly, which sometimes opens too widely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and some have had hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address any delays or difficulties.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a structural heart abnormality and requires close monitoring and management with a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges during mealtime and struggles with feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which can be distressing for everyone involved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV up to very high levels, indicating a potential issue with her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit extremely close to the television or when reading books, raising concerns about her eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip rather easily, requiring frequent dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) in secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes struggles to find the right words when trying to communicate, indicating a potential issue with speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and may have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor and manage the patient's hearing health.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor and manage the patient's vision health.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor and manage the patient's heart health.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor and manage the patient's skeletal health.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and well-being.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with food textures and can be fussy about what she eats, requiring patience and creativity at mealtime.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient took longer than expected to reach certain developmental milestones like walking or sitting and has required physical therapy to support progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks for repetitions because she didn't quite catch what was said, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient mentions that things look blurry to her, especially when trying to focus on something far away, prompting regular eye checks.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with one of her heart valves, requiring regular check-ups with a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, having trouble passing stools regularly and often complains of feeling bloated or uncomfortable after meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination challenges, appearing less steady on her feet compared to her peers, especially in certain situations like running or engaging in sports.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is easily overwhelmed by loud noises, becomes frustrated in crowded or noisy environments, and has difficulty with background noise.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs her eyes, especially when trying to focus on something, indicating possible vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than her peers, affecting her smile and bite, and requiring close monitoring and good oral hygiene practices.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to lag behind her peers developmentally, with certain skills and milestones taking longer to achieve than expected, prompting discussions about possible interventions or support systems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but possibly requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and possibly coordination challenges, indicating potential behavioural differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and oral hygiene.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially given the patient's sensitivity to noise.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and address any vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart valve issue.
* Consideration of a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
* Referral for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's developmental needs.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if the patient's height is below the 2nd centile.
* Regular check-ups with a cardiologist to manage the heart condition.
* Dietary adjustments and possible interventions to manage constipation.
* Support systems or interventions to help bridge developmental gaps.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted rather quickly when engaging in physical activities, and even simple play can leave her feeling drained after a short while.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond immediately when called, appearing distracted or not paying attention, which can be concerning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs her eyes when trying to focus on something, especially when watching TV or playing with toys, and her eyes seem to get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and tends to avoid eating meats or crunchy vegetables because they're difficult for her to chew.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school, and some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with shorter fingers on one hand, which may affect her development and dexterity over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel health

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality, requiring cautious physical activity levels and regular check-ups with her cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion to certain foods, making mealtime challenging, and requires gradual introduction to various foods to help her become more comfortable with different textures and tastes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a small number needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems less coordinated than her peers in physical activities, with slower-developing balance and motor skills, and struggles with expressing herself clearly, leading to frustration during communication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have developmental delay, with the degree ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, which sometimes causes her to tilt her head to see properly, and may have hearing difficulties, as she doesn't always respond immediately when called.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many have required multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, which affects her vision, and her optometrist is monitoring the situation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with some requiring patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, making her teeth more prone to cavities, and requires regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups, with some needing specialist SEN dentists.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's communication challenges and slower-developing motor skills may impact her educational progress and social interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school, but some requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans due to more significant learning difficulties.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with expressing herself clearly, leading to frustration during communication, and has slower-developing motor skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved 5th fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine, with a small number having hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent dental issues
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing concerns
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor and address vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental and communication challenges
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) if clinical concerns arise

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, and the parents work closely with her neurologist to manage them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes asks her parents to repeat things because she didn't quite catch what they said the first time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia and needs glasses to see clearly.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular monitoring of seizure activity and adjustment of anti-epileptic treatments as needed

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires regular check-ups for monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gains weight slowly compared to her friends, which has been a concern for the parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient took a bit longer to learn how to walk and sit than other kids, but is otherwise doing well.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and developmental delay is common.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear once, which was treated, and now her hearing seems fine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which is corrected with glasses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes complains of tooth pain when eating cold foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, for which she is receiving physical therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth pain and dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing loss
* Regular eyesight reviews to monitor vision problems
* Regular check-ups to monitor the septal defect
* Physical therapy to help manage scoliosis
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily when playing with friends or engaging in prolonged physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Constipation has been an ongoing issue, and various diets and strategies have been tried to help regulate bowel movements.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epilepsy, and her parents work closely with neurologists to manage her condition and reduce seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear last year, which was a concern due to fluid buildup, and after treatment, her hearing improved significantly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means she needs glasses to see distant objects clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's front teeth are larger than average, similar to what has been seen in some of her family members.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is behind in speech development for her age, and clarity is sometimes an issue when she tries to communicate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and enamel health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delay and behavioural differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular monitoring for signs of tethered cord, such as sacral dimple or asymmetric gait, and referral for MRI if clinical concerns arise.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in his heart that was diagnosed early on. Regular cardiology check-ups help monitor the situation and adjust treatment as necessary to ensure it doesn't impact his daily life too significantly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had trouble feeding due to reflux and digestive discomfort as an infant. However, those issues resolved themselves over time and now his eating habits are mostly normal.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects muscle tone and can make movements slightly more difficult. Physical therapy sessions have been very helpful in managing this condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported as having seizures, of varying types. Seizures typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media when he was younger. Fortunately, after treatment and follow-up care, the condition cleared up and hasn't caused any lasting issues with his hearing. He also has a squint, which affects his ability to focus on objects directly in front of him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple aeration tube (grommet) insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear, and some have still required hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, which affects his ability to focus on objects directly in front of him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak tooth enamel. As a result, extra precautions have been taken to prevent decay and strengthen them through fluoride treatments and good oral hygiene practices.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns. Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has taken longer to reach developmental milestones than peers. Despite these challenges, with support and therapies, he's making steady progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has taken longer to reach developmental milestones than peers. Despite these challenges, with support and therapies, he's making steady progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD or anxiety. Medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than typical for his age group.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage weak tooth enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for any hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiology check-ups to monitor the septal defect in the heart
* Physical therapy sessions to manage hypotonia
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if necessary
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that was diagnosed early on and requires regular monitoring by specialists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation if he doesn't drink enough water and has trouble passing stool. Some foods also seem to disagree with him, giving him bad diarrhea.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in children with KBG syndrome, and some may require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other children, even on flat ground, and has trouble with clarity when trying to talk.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in his ear and pulls at his ear when it bothers him, especially during flights or when he has a cold.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains that things look blurry sometimes, especially when he's tired or after playing video games.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, even when eating normal foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's learning may be affected by his vision and hearing problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble with clarity when trying to talk and gets frustrated when not understood.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor for heart conditions
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for skeletal abnormalities
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and behavior
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) if clinical concerns arise

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that requires management and monitoring by a cardiologist to prevent significant impact on daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, some of which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion and is particular about what he eats, making meal times challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding. A lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and is being monitored and treated by a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in some cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing clearly and often asks people to repeat themselves, indicating a hearing issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board at school, especially with small letters or from a distance, indicating a vision problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has frequent tooth issues, including cavities, and requires regular dental monitoring and treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups. Large front teeth are also a common feature.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many attend mainstream primary school but may transfer to special schooling or require Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay and behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers. A small number have hip dysplasia or experience delayed closure of the soft spot on the head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and treat tooth issues.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to manage heart abnormalities.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had trouble with feeding as a baby, having difficulty latching on and getting frustrated during meals. However, this has improved significantly since then.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epilepsy and has seizures that can be scary to watch. He works closely with neurologists to manage them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported as having seizures, of varying types. Seizures typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond right away when called, which has raised concerns about his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple aeration tube (grommet) insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means his eyes are crossed. It's been noticeable since he was little and might affect his vision or cause discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's front teeth are larger than usual, which was noticed when they first came in. The dentist recommends monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel. Regular dental check-ups are important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is taking longer than his peers to reach certain developmental milestones. He also struggles with finding the right words sometimes, which affects his ability to communicate clearly.

The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
